It produced no evidence and does not affect the rendered run.. Judge: The commercial-looking frames win all four pairs clearly, and none is close enough to call indistinguishable. Two of them carry a logo; I ignored it and judged only what was rendered. The in-development frames do capture the landmark silhouettes: the three-tower hotel with its sky deck, the lotus museum, the glass domes, the tree sculptures, the helix bridge and the lion statue. Pairs 2 and 3 also get to passable warm lighting. But every in-development frame fails on the same four things. Life: no other people, cars or boats. Density: copied, sparse trees, flat lawns and empty plazas. Material work: repeated stripe facades, clean untextured tubes, flat water without reflections, and untextured placeholder boxes in pair 4. Atmosphere: either a flat uniform veil or no haze at all, never a graded fade with distance. The camera work also misses: pair 1's helicopter is a speck, and pair 2 leaves an empty foreground. The stronger frames have dated, low-resolution textures themselves (blurry asphalt and a flat sky in pair 3), so the gap is mostly content, life and staging rather than raw rendering fidelity. Only two frames genuinely wow me: the close helicopter shot (pair 1 A) and the backlit hilltop sign overlook (pair 4 B). Fixes in priority order: fill scenes with pedestrians, traffic and boats; replace placeholder blocks and copied vegetation; add weathering, reflections and haze that fades with distance; frame hero subjects up close.
